item.title: Entrepreneurship, Creative Destruction, and Growth: Enriching the Aghion-Howitt Tradition
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks research that advances Schumpeterian economics by connecting entrepreneurship and firm dynamics at multiple levels of analysis—from individual ventures and firm behavior to regional innovation ecosystems and broader institutional environments. The special issue builds on the Aghion-Howitt tradition of studying how entrepreneurial activity drives creative destruction and economic growth.

Submissions should explore not just business creation but also how firms scale after entry, exit markets, and reallocate resources through competitive processes that ultimately generate productivity improvements. Additionally, the editors welcome research that enriches the Aghion-Howitt framework by incorporating contemporary insights and theoretical approaches from entrepreneurship scholarship.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • New venture formation
  • Post-entry scaling
  • Firm displacement and exit
  • Reallocation dynamics
  • Innovation and productivity growth
  • Schumpeterian economics
  • Multi-level research (micro, meso, macro)
  • Regional ecosystems
  • Industrial structure
  • Institutional configurations
  • Policy regimes
  • Entrepreneurship research frameworks

Timeline

  • November 1, 2026: Submission deadline
